reasoning: Alaska’s current Senate race is best described as a toss-up, with recent polling in late June showing Mary Peltola slightly ahead in one survey and Dan Sullivan slightly ahead in another, leaving the race effectively even overall. The statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is R+9, indicating a strong Republican lean even though the 2026 Senate contest remains competitive.

sources.name: New York Times / Siena College
sources.details: A New York Times/Siena College poll of likely Alaska voters found Dan Sullivan leading Mary Peltola 47% to 45%, a 2-point Republican edge.

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research
sources.details: A later-referenced Alaska Survey Research poll found Mary Peltola ahead of Dan Sullivan 49.4% to 44.2%, a 5.2-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: Newsweek / Alaska Survey Research
sources.details: Newsweek reported another Alaska Survey Research poll of 1,528 registered voters showing a very close race at 50.9% for Tom Begich to 49.1% for Bernadette Wilson, which is not the Senate race and is therefore only contextual.

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax’s aggregate for the Alaska Senate race showed an average of 45.8% D to 46.7% R, a 0.9-point Republican edge.

sources.name: The Alaska Story / PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax forecast Republican Dan Sullivan over Democrat Mary Peltola by 5.8 percentage points.
